science.name: Stop A: ridge and hollow
science.why: Bedrock ridge next to a sand-filled hollow. Compare ridge and hollow material.

science.name: Stop B: fractured bedrock
science.why: Wide exposure of fractured bedrock plates between ridges.

science.name: Stop C: Nevado Sajama drill area
science.why: Where Curiosity drilled a boxwork ridge in November 2025. Sample the same ridge.

radiation.source: Curiosity RAD surface average, Aug 2012 to Jun 2013 (Hassler et al., Science, 2014)
radiation.note: Published long-term average, not a reading for these sols.
radiation.earth_source: Earth: 2.4 mSv/year world average natural background (UNSCEAR)
radiation.storm_note: Solar storms can raise the dose sharply for hours. Live solar-storm alerts are not included in this replay.

assumptions: Walking speed 0.5 m/s is an assumption for a suited astronaut on rough ground.
Distances are straight lines between rover stops; the real path is longer.
The re-route bend is illustrative: the scout picks its path in the photo, which is not geolocated.
Weather is the Curiosity REMS reading for the sol the rover reached each stop.
Each stop's status is for the view ahead, toward the next stop. Other directions are shown for looking around.
